title: The storage rooms and their fittings
summary: Storage in R.E.P.O. is a room the build fits out: a metal shelf, an art divider and a big pipe, archive boxes, a broom and a bucket, ceiling pipes, and a gold plaque that says Storage Room.
body: Storage in R.E.P.O. is a room the build fits out rather than a bare corner. The museum storage room is named as a set of its own, with floors, ceilings and walls named for it, so the room can be cut to the space a level has left.
The room carries fittings of its own: a metal storage shelf, an art divider and a big pipe, which is why a storage room reads as somewhere things are kept rather than as empty floor.

The boxes are named one by one and then as a group. Three archive boxes are named separately and an archive box set is named beside them, so what a player sees stacked in the corner is a set of pieces rather than one crate repeated.
There is a cleaning corner as well: a broom, a bucket and the bucket's own items are named for the storage room, which is why the room can be kept tidy without borrowing a shop's fittings.
The ceiling is fitted, too. Ceiling pipes are named for the room beside its other pieces, so the top of a storage space is built rather than left as the underside of the floor above.
Not everything stored there is a box. A bust and a cone are named for the storage room as well, so a player searching one can find an ornament or a traffic cone standing where the crates are.

The rooms are signed and they are not all the same room. The wizard theme hangs a gold plaque reading Storage Room, and it names a cauldron storage of its own beside it, while a shop module can be a storage room in its own right. That is why storage is worth reading by theme: what is kept there changes with the level.
What this entry does not tell you: how much a storage room holds, which valuables spawn in one, or how many the generator places. We have not verified those, so we do not print them.
